writeup: TIC 318232056 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.9826 days. The primary eclipse causes the star to dim by 5.91%, while a secondary eclipse was detected at high significance (6.2 sigma) near orbital phase 0.49, suggesting the two stars are of comparable brightness. Automated analysis of TESS photometry yielded a strong detection signal of 239.7 in the box least-squares periodogram, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal's location near the target coordinates with a peak signal-to-noise of 18.2 and a centroid offset of 1.2 arcsec. This candidate does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, and the machine-learning screening model assigned it a score of 0.72, indicating properties consistent with a genuine eclipsing pair.
